title: Clonable Front Ends & dApp UIs — verified catalogue for MELEK / PRANA / KULA / SoapBox
author: Claude Code research pass for the Van Kush / MELEK Bot repo
period: 2025-2026 (all entries verified against the GitHub API on 2026-09-05)
source: Direct verification: GitHub REST API (repos, /license, /contents, /releases) and raw.githubusercontent.com LICENSE and README fetches. No entry is included that could not be fetched.
overview: A catalogue of real, fetched-and-confirmed open-source front ends this repo could clone or crib from, covering wallet UIs, block explorers, NFT mint/marketplace pages, DEX/swap interfaces, launchpad/staking/faucet pages, mining-pool front ends, and wallet-connect layers. Every repository below was fetched: existence, last push date, archived flag and the EXACT licence text were confirmed, not assumed. Several widely-repeated licence claims turned out to be stale — Blockscout, Reown AppKit and WalletConnect all relicensed away from open source in 2025-2026, and Uniswap's front end, several 'open source' explorers and yiimp are all copyleft or unlicensed. Those are called out as landmines rather than buried.

verification_method.what_was_checked: repo exists; full_name after redirects; SPDX licence id; the first lines of the actual LICENSE file when GitHub reported NOASSERTION or none; last push date; archived flag; latest release tag and date; and for the ambiguous cases, the raw LICENSE at a specific tag.
verification_method.excluded: Anything that 404'd or could not have its licence read was dropped rather than guessed. Repos dropped for this reason during research included several search-result NFT/launchpad templates with no licence and near-zero adoption.

house_style_constraint.what_this_repo_is: Plain ESM .mjs, no build step, no framework. Server modules export handler(req,res). Tests run offline under node --test with injectable fetch. Front ends are static HTML plus hand-written .mjs modules (site/hathor-live/, pool/www/) with cryptographic primitives vendored as small clean-room ESM files (pool/www/walletgen/vendor/).
house_style_constraint.what_already_exists: pool/www — browser miner, in-browser walletgen (ZEPH/XMR/EVM), My Coins, PWA. kulaswap/ — a hand-written DEX/CDP/staking/farm UI over ethers 6, already targeting PRANA chainId 712217. site/hathor-live/ — chat, sessions, reports. integrations/ — ~100 shared reader modules including melek-theme.mjs and ecosystem-nav.mjs.
house_style_constraint.the_honest_cost_of_react: Every entry marked 'React/Next, heavy port' means adopting a second toolchain — package manager lockfile, bundler, its own CI, and a dependency surface that this repo currently does not have and that its offline node --test suite cannot exercise. That is a real, ongoing cost, not a one-time port. Where a React project is recommended below, it is recommended as a SEPARATE deployment or as a design reference, never as something to merge into the Bot repo's build.
house_style_constraint.what_drop_in_means_here: A single self-contained HTML file, or an ESM module importable from a <script type=module> with no bundler, or a pre-built artifact configured at runtime by a JSON/JS config file.

licence_landmines_2025_2026.headline: Three of the most-recommended projects in this space stopped being open source in 2025-2026, and most published guides have not caught up.

blockscout_relicensed.now: LicenseRef-Blockscout, a bespoke proprietary source-available licence, Effective Date 2026-04-22, Version 1.0, licensor Blockscout Limited (Seychelles), with a separate 'Commercial Licence' tier.
blockscout_relicensed.proof: raw LICENSE at tag v6.10.1 begins 'GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3'; raw LICENSE at main begins 'SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-Blockscout / Effective Date: 2026-04-22'.
blockscout_relicensed.practical_effect: Any plan to 'just run Blockscout, it's GPL' must either pin <= v6.10.1 (and accept GPL-3.0) or read the new licence in full. Current HEAD is not open source.

walletconnect_reown_relicensed.now: Reown Community License Agreement (release 2025-08-25) and WalletConnect Community License Agreement (release 2025-08-20).
worst_terms: Reown claims ownership of your modifications and derivative works, and you assign those rights to them.
A MATERIAL CONDITION that all use and derivative works must connect to Reown's proprietary gateway infrastructure; circumventing it, or telling your users to, is a breach.
Free use capped at 2,500,000 monthly RPCs or 500 monthly active users; beyond that a paid commercial licence is required.
Mandatory 'Portions (c) 2025 Reown, Inc. All Rights Reserved' notice plus their branding on redistribution.
walletconnect_reown_relicensed.practical_effect: Incompatible with a self-sovereign multi-chain stack. It also contaminates the DEFAULT configuration of RainbowKit, ConnectKit, web3-onboard and thirdweb, all of which are themselves permissively licensed but ship WalletConnect transports for mobile wallets. Injected/EIP-6963-only configurations avoid it entirely.

copyleft_that_actually_bites_a_hosted_fr.agpl: AGPL-3.0 is the one that triggers on hosting: OpenZeppelin/contracts-wizard and rotki are AGPL. Self-hosting a modified copy obliges you to publish your source.
copyleft_that_actually_bites_a_hosted_fr.gpl: GPL-2.0/GPL-3.0 (Uniswap/interface, cowprotocol/cowswap, DefiLlama/chainlist, lidofinance/ethereum-staking-widget, dvandal/cryptonote-nodejs-pool, etclabscore/open-etc-pool, sammy007/open-ethereum-pool, blinkhash, s-nomp, NOMP, blockscout <= v6.10.1). GPL has no network clause, but a web front end DISTRIBUTES its JavaScript bundle to every visitor, and that is distribution. Treat GPL obligations on a cloned front end as live.
copyleft_that_actually_bites_a_hosted_fr.busl: BUSL-1.1 (Uniswap v3-core, Uniswap v4-core, Dune spellbook) is not open source at HEAD; it converts to GPL on a delay. Note that Uniswap v4-core has no root LICENSE file at all — the SPDX header is inside the .sol sources, so GitHub's licence detector reports nothing.
copyleft_that_actually_bites_a_hosted_fr.sspl: SSPL-1.0 (EthVM) is not OSI-approved and is aggressively viral for anything offered as a service.
copyleft_that_actually_bites_a_hosted_fr.lgpl: LGPL-3.0 (web3/web3.js, cubedro/eth-netstats). LGPL is fine when dynamically linked, but a single bundled JS artifact is closer to static linking and drags in relinking obligations.

no_licence_at_all.meaning: No LICENSE file means all rights reserved by default. These are NOT safe to clone, however widely they are deployed.
repos: steemit/condenser — no LICENSE or COPYING in the repo root (verified). Use openhive-network/condenser, which IS MIT.
openhive-network/block_explorer_ui — no licence file. The only maintained modern Graphene explorer UI, and legally unclonable.
openhive-network/haf_block_explorer, openhive-network/denser, openhive-network/wallet, openhive-network/clive — same problem.
tpruvot/yiimp — 550 stars, very widely deployed as a mining pool, no licence file.

proprietary_but_widely_assumed_open: MetaMask/metamask-extension and MetaMask/metamask-sdk — 'Copyright ConsenSys Software Inc. 2022. All rights reserved.'
trezor/connect — Trezor Reference Source License (T-RSL), and archived.
web3labs/chainlens-free (ex-epirus-free) — a Web3 Labs Ltd commercial EULA, despite appearing in 'open source explorer' roundups.

wallet_uis.closest_to_house_style: iancoleman/bip39 — a single self-contained HTML file doing client-side key derivation with vendored crypto and no toolchain. This is structurally the same thing pool/www/walletgen already is, which means it is the right place to crib UI affordances from rather than a project to import.
wallet_uis.what_this_repo_already_has: pool/www/walletgen generates ZEPH/XMR/EVM keys entirely in-browser from clean-room vendored primitives (keccak, ed25519, cn-base58, cn-address, Monero wordlist, mnemonic, secp256k1), each verified against published test vectors in walletgen.test.mjs. Nothing in this catalogue improves on that for the chains already covered.
gaps_worth_filling: SIGNING. The vendored secp256k1.mjs is derivation-only. paulmillr/noble-curves (MIT, audited, zero-dep ESM) is the drop-in if client-side signing is ever needed.

HARDWARE WALLET. There is no ledger/trezor path today. The only permissive option is @ledgerhq/hw-transport-webhid + @ledgerhq/hw-app-eth from LedgerHQ/ledger-live (MIT). Trezor's connect library is under a non-permissive reference-source licence and is archived.
SEND/RECEIVE/SWAP UX. MyEtherWallet (MIT, actively maintained) is the reference to study; it is Vue/Nuxt and not portable here.
wallet_uis.do_not_touch: MetaMask (proprietary). Rabby is MIT if a branded extension is ever genuinely wanted.

for_prana_evm_chainid_712217.first_choice: Alethio/ethereum-lite-explorer (MIT). Client-side only, speaks plain Ethereum JSON-RPC, needs no indexer, no archive node and no backend, and is configured at RUNTIME by a config.json — so the pre-built Docker image can be pointed at a PRANA RPC without ever running its build. Cost: last release 2020, so no EIP-1559 fee UI and no ERC-20 decoding out of the box.
for_prana_evm_chainid_712217.second_choice: xops/expedition (Apache-2.0). Same architecture — React SPA over raw JSON-RPC — with a cleaner licence than GPL, but stale since 2021.
for_prana_evm_chainid_712217.best_maintained_but_conditional: otterscan/otterscan (MIT, release v2.11.0 in Nov 2025). Excellent and alive, but it REQUIRES an Erigon archive node exposing custom ots_* RPC methods. If PRANA nodes are not Erigon, this needs an ots_* shim written first — that is the real cost, not the UI.
for_prana_evm_chainid_712217.if_more_than_raw_rpc_is_needed: ponder-sh/ponder (MIT) as the indexer, serving a plain API that a hand-written .mjs page in house style can consume. This keeps the front end in-repo and in-style while getting token transfers, holder lists and NFT ownership.
for_prana_evm_chainid_712217.verification_layer: argotorg/sourcify (MIT) for verified contract sources; pairs with any of the above.
for_prana_evm_chainid_712217.avoid: Blockscout at HEAD (proprietary since 2026-04-22), EthVM (SSPL), chainlens-free (commercial EULA), beaconcha.in (GPL-3.0 and consensus-layer-only).
for_prana_evm_chainid_712217.cheapest_win_of_all: PRANA is NOT in ethereum-lists/chains — _data/chains/eip155-712217.json returns 404 (verified). That registry is MIT and is consumed by chainlist.org and by wallet/explorer network pickers. One JSON pull request makes PRANA discoverable and 'Add to MetaMask'-able everywhere, with zero front-end code.

for_melek_graphene_steem_fork.hard_finding: There is NO maintained, permissively-licensed Graphene/Steem-family block explorer front end. openhive-network/block_explorer_ui is the only modern one and it has no licence file at all; its haf_block_explorer backend is the same. Both also assume hived + HAF on Postgres, which a Steem fork would need porting to regardless.
for_melek_graphene_steem_fork.recommendation: Do not try to clone one. Build MELEK's explorer as a house-style .mjs surface over this repo's existing steemd reader (integrations/) — block/tx/account/witness pages are a small amount of code against condenser_api, and the repo already renders comparable pages for witness.melek.salon/hathor.
for_melek_graphene_steem_fork.what_is_legally_reusable: openhive-network/condenser (MIT) for the social front end, openhive-network/wax and hive-js (MIT) for protocol calls, hive-keychain-extension (MIT) as the working reference for browser key custody and a site-callable sign API.

nft_marketplace_and_mint.protocol_layer: ProjectOpenSea/seaport (MIT) plus ProjectOpenSea/seaport-js (MIT). seaport-js is built on ethers, which this repo already depends on at 6.16.0 — that makes it the least-friction route to real listing/offer/fulfil flows from a hand-written page. OpenSea's own SDK is MIT but talks to OpenSea's hosted API, which will never index PRANA; a self-deployed Seaport plus seaport-js is the usable half.
nft_marketplace_and_mint.contract_layer: OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts (MIT) for ERC721/ERC1155 and access control on any mint or breeding contract.
nft_marketplace_and_mint.full_stack_forkable: scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2 (MIT, actively maintained) is the standard forkable mint/collection dApp starting point, and thirdweb-dev/js (Apache-2.0) bundles prebuilt drop/marketplace/staking contracts with connect UI. BOTH are Next.js/React/full-toolchain — a genuinely heavy lift here. If the breeding/genetics game gets built, give it its own deployment rather than importing a bundler into the Bot repo.
nft_marketplace_and_mint.design_reference_only: kodadot/nft-gallery (MIT) is a complete generative-art marketplace with collection and mint pages — but it was ARCHIVED in 2025 and targets Polkadot/RMRK, not EVM. Read it for collection-page and trait/genetics information architecture.
nft_marketplace_and_mint.landmine: OpenZeppelin/contracts-wizard is AGPL-3.0. The MIT contracts it emits are fine; self-hosting a fork of the wizard app is the AGPL trigger.

dex_swap.the_licensing_headline: Uniswap's front end is GPL-3.0 and its v3/v4 cores are BUSL-1.1. Sushi 2.0 (sushi-labs/sushiswap) is MIT and actively maintained. If any real swap-UI code is going to be lifted, lift it from Sushi.
dex_swap.what_this_repo_already_has: kulaswap/ is a hand-written, offline-tested DEX/CDP/farm/staking UI over ethers, already bound to PRANA chainId 712217 with a zero-address 'is it live' guard before any tx is built. It carries no copyleft. Preserving that clean-licence position is worth more than any UI code in this section.
dex_swap.embeddable_widget: lifinance/widget (Apache-2.0, actively maintained) is the best-licensed embeddable swap/bridge widget and can be dropped in as a pre-built bundle. Caveat: it routes through LI.FI's hosted API, so it is a third-party service dependency — appropriate for a bridge page, wrong for a self-sovereign KULA swap.
dex_swap.safe_to_integrate: Uniswap/permit2 (MIT) for gasless approvals; Uniswap/sdk-core (MIT, archived) for price/currency primitives. Using a GPL contract's ABI to build calldata — which kulaswap already does — is not the same as forking the source.
dex_swap.avoid: aave/interface is 'All Rights Reserved (c) Aave Labs' and is not a legal base for a lending/CDP UI. compound-finance/palisade is GPL-3.0 and written in Elm.

launchpad_staking_faucet.faucet: chainflag/eth-faucet (MIT, maintained, 573 stars) is the cleanest self-hostable EVM faucet: configurable RPC and chainId, built for custom testnets, shipped as a Go binary or Docker image. Critically, the funding key stays SERVER-SIDE in the Go process, which matches this repo's key-custody rule. Its Svelte front end is small enough to discard and replace with a house-style static page against the same backend.
launchpad_staking_faucet.staking_dashboards: No permissively-licensed general staking dashboard is worth cloning. lidofinance/ethereum-staking-widget is GPL-3.0 and Lido-contract-specific. kulaswap/kula-stake.mjs, soapbox-staking.mjs and sprana-staking.mjs already cover this ground in house style.
launchpad_staking_faucet.launchpad_presale: There is no credible, maintained, permissively-licensed presale/launchpad front end. Search results in this category are near-universally unlicensed, abandoned, or single-author templates with no adoption, and were excluded rather than cited. thirdweb-dev/js (Apache-2.0) is the only serious option, and it is React plus hosted-service coupling. Building a presale page in house style against an OpenZeppelin-based sale contract is less work than porting one.
launchpad_staking_faucet.account_abstraction: alchemyplatform/aa-sdk (MIT) and pimlicolabs/permissionless.js (MIT) are both permissive and relevant to the KULA paymaster work, but both presume PRANA deploys an ERC-4337 EntryPoint and runs a bundler.

mining_pool_frontends.what_is_actually_better_than_pool_www: Honestly: not much, and nothing that is both better AND cleanly licensed. pool/www already does browser mining, in-browser walletgen, My Coins, a spend-lock and a PWA — which is more than any of these ship.
mining_pool_frontends.best_stylistic_match: dvandal/cryptonote-nodejs-pool's website_example/ is plain index.html + config.js + js/ + themes/ + lang/ with no build step — the same shape as pool/www, with the miner-stats/payments/blocks page layout and i18n already factored out. LANDMINE: it is GPL-2.0. Read the layout and the i18n structure, then re-implement; do not copy files in.
mining_pool_frontends.best_licensed_backend: MoneroOcean/nodejs-pool (MIT, pushed 2026-09-04) is the most actively maintained CryptoNote/RandomX pool backend and supports algo auto-switching — directly relevant to the pool's RandomX/Monero-stagenet side, and MIT means it is the one pool codebase that could actually be vendored. Its front end (Snipa22/poolui, MIT) is AngularJS from 2018 and should be treated as API documentation-by-example, not as a UI.
mining_pool_frontends.if_prana_ever_needs_a_pool: etclabscore/open-etc-pool (GPL-3.0, maintained) is the living EVM pool; oliverw/miningcore (MIT) supports EVM chains but was archived in 2023. MIT-but-archived vs GPL-but-alive is the actual choice.
mining_pool_frontends.do_not_clone: tpruvot/yiimp (no licence file despite 550 stars and wide deployment) and notgiven688/webminerpool (no licence file, archived).

wallet_connect_layers.the_lightest_possible_vanilla_option: EIP-6963 provider discovery, hand-written. It is roughly thirty lines: dispatch `eip6963:requestProvider`, collect `eip6963:announceProvider` events into a list, let the user pick, then hand the chosen provider to `new ethers.BrowserProvider(...)`. No bundler, no framework, no new dependency. wevm/mipd (MIT, ~2KB, dependency-free ESM) is the same thing packaged, and is small enough to vendor as one file next to pool/www/walletgen/vendor/.
wallet_connect_layers.concrete_gap_in_this_repo: kulaswap/app.mjs currently does `if (!window.ethereum)` then `new ethers.BrowserProvider(window.ethereum)` — the legacy single-injected-provider path. When a visitor has more than one wallet extension installed, that silently connects to whichever one won the injection race. EIP-6963 is the fix and it costs almost nothing here.
wallet_connect_layers.already_correct: ethers 6.16.0 is already a dependency, is MIT, and ships a browser ESM build. Nothing in this section justifies replacing it. viem and ox are MIT and excellent, but both realistically want a bundler.
wallet_connect_layers.if_a_connect_modal_is_ever_wanted: thirdweb-dev/web3-onboard (MIT) is the least React-bound option; family/connectkit (BSD-2-Clause) and rainbow-me/rainbowkit (MIT) are React. All three are permissively licensed THEMSELVES but ship WalletConnect transports by default for mobile wallets, and WalletConnect is no longer permissively licensed — configure injected/EIP-6963 connectors only.

genuinely_new_2025_2026.the_relicensing_wave: The single most important 2025-2026 development for this lane is not a new UI — it is that Blockscout (2026-04-22), Reown AppKit (2025-08-25) and WalletConnect (2025-08-20) all moved off open-source licences. Any guide or LLM answer written before those dates will confidently give the old licences. Verify before adopting.
genuinely_new_2025_2026.farcaster_mini_apps: farcasterxyz/miniapps (MIT, actively maintained). The notable new dApp-UI form factor: a plain web page rendered inside a social feed with a wallet already injected by the host. Its constraints — one page, host-provided wallet, no build assumptions — line up with this repo's house style unusually well. A KULA swap or a mint page could ship as a mini app with very little new machinery.
genuinely_new_2025_2026.eip_7702_and_smart_accounts: EIP-7702 turned EOAs into programmable accounts in 2025. ithacaxyz/porto (Apache-2.0) was a leading experiment and is now ARCHIVED; the live permissive options are pimlicolabs/permissionless.js and alchemyplatform/aa-sdk, both MIT, both requiring bundler infrastructure on the chain.
genuinely_new_2025_2026.ox: wevm/ox (MIT) — the tree-shakeable, framework-free EVM standard library that viem is being rebuilt on. The most house-style-compatible of the new primitive layers, if ethers is ever outgrown.
genuinely_new_2025_2026.what_did_not_change: There is still no lightweight, actively-maintained, permissively-licensed self-hostable EVM explorer. The good ones are either stale (Alethio 2020, Expedition 2021), backend-coupled (Otterscan needs Erigon), or relicensed (Blockscout). This remains a genuine gap.

top_five_to_clone_first.name: Alethio/ethereum-lite-explorer
top_five_to_clone_first.why: A PRANA block explorer with no backend, no indexer and no rebuild — config.json points the pre-built client-side SPA at any JSON-RPC node. MIT, so nothing infects this repo. Ship it behind a subdomain; accept that it is a 2020-era UI.
top_five_to_clone_first.landmine: None. The landmine is the obvious alternative: Blockscout is no longer GPL/open source as of 2026-04-22.

top_five_to_clone_first.name: EIP-6963 discovery via wevm/mipd (or ~30 hand-written lines)
top_five_to_clone_first.why: Fixes a real, present bug: kulaswap/app.mjs grabs window.ethereum and connects to whichever extension won the injection race. ~2KB, dependency-free ESM, vendorable as one file, zero toolchain. Highest value-per-byte in this entire catalogue.
top_five_to_clone_first.landmine: Do NOT reach for Reown AppKit / Web3Modal to solve this — it stopped being Apache-2.0 on 2025-08-25 and now requires routing through Reown's gateway.

top_five_to_clone_first.name: ethereum-lists/chains (a data PR, not a clone)
top_five_to_clone_first.why: VERIFIED: PRANA chainId 712217 is not registered — eip155-712217.json is a 404. One JSON file propagates PRANA into chainlist.org and into wallet and explorer network pickers. No front-end code, and it is a prerequisite for anyone finding the chain at all.
top_five_to_clone_first.landmine: Do not fork DefiLlama/chainlist itself — that UI is GPL-3.0. You only need the MIT data repo it consumes.

top_five_to_clone_first.name: chainflag/eth-faucet
top_five_to_clone_first.why: Self-hostable PRANA faucet: configurable RPC/chainId, single Go binary or Docker image, funding key stays server-side — which is exactly this repo's key-custody boundary. Keep the Go backend, replace the Svelte page with a house-style static page.
top_five_to_clone_first.landmine: None. Note it does need a backend process; it is not a static page.

top_five_to_clone_first.name: ProjectOpenSea/seaport-js (+ seaport, + OpenZeppelin contracts)
top_five_to_clone_first.why: The NFT mint/marketplace path that does not require importing a React toolchain: seaport-js is built on ethers, which is already a dependency, so listing/offer/fulfil flows can be driven from a hand-written .mjs page against a self-deployed Seaport on PRANA.
top_five_to_clone_first.landmine: OpenSea's own opensea-sdk is MIT but talks to OpenSea's hosted API, which will never index PRANA. And if the full scaffold-eth-2 route is taken for the breeding game instead, give it a separate deployment — it is a whole second toolchain.

explicitly_rejected.name: blockscout/blockscout at HEAD
explicitly_rejected.reason: Relicensed 2026-04-22 to a proprietary Blockscout Licence. Pin <= v6.10.1 for GPL-3.0, or read the new terms.

explicitly_rejected.name: reown-com/appkit and WalletConnect/walletconnect-monorepo
explicitly_rejected.reason: 2025 Community Licences: derivative-work IP assignment to Reown, a mandatory-connection-to-their-gateway clause, and MAU/RPC caps.

explicitly_rejected.name: Uniswap/interface
explicitly_rejected.reason: GPL-3.0, and an Nx/React-Native-Web monorepo. Use sushi-labs/sushiswap (MIT) if any swap UI code is to be lifted.

explicitly_rejected.name: steemit/condenser, openhive-network/block_explorer_ui, tpruvot/yiimp
explicitly_rejected.reason: No LICENSE file — all rights reserved by default, however widely deployed.

explicitly_rejected.name: MetaMask/metamask-extension, MetaMask/metamask-sdk, aave/interface, web3labs/chainlens-free, trezor/connect
explicitly_rejected.reason: Proprietary licences, routinely mislabelled as open source.

explicitly_rejected.name: EthVM/EthVM
explicitly_rejected.reason: SSPL-1.0 — not OSI-approved, and viral against exactly the hosted-service use case a chain explorer is.

explicitly_rejected.name: OpenZeppelin/contracts-wizard (self-hosted fork)
explicitly_rejected.reason: AGPL-3.0 — the one copyleft licence whose network clause fires on hosting. Use the public instance.

explicitly_rejected.name: Unverifiable presale/launchpad and NFT-mint templates from search
explicitly_rejected.reason: Unlicensed, abandoned, or single-author with no adoption. Excluded rather than cited, per the no-fabricated-citations rule.

catalog.name: iancoleman/bip39 (BIP39 mnemonic tool)
catalog.last_active: 2024-04-28 (last push); no release since 2021; 4.3k stars; not archived
catalog.build_complexity: vanilla, drop-in — ONE self-contained HTML file plus jQuery/vendored crypto; no build step at all
catalog.works_with_prana: yes — derives BIP44 m/44'/60' EVM keys; PRANA is just another EVM coin type
catalog.works_with_melek: partial — BIP39/BIP44 is not Graphene key derivation; MELEK keys are the brain-key/sha256 role-key scheme
catalog.notes: The single closest existing project to this repo's house style: a static page that does client-side key generation with vendored crypto and no toolchain. Its self-contained build (`bip39-standalone.html`) is exactly the pattern `pool/www/walletgen/` already follows. Best source to crib UI affordances (entropy display, derivation-path table, per-account address list) for the existing walletgen.

catalog.name: paulmillr/scure-bip39
catalog.build_complexity: vanilla, drop-in — audited ESM, zero deps, browser-importable
catalog.notes: Audited minimal BIP39. If walletgen ever needs a second opinion against its clean-room `vendor/mnemonic.mjs`, this is the reference to test-vector against.

catalog.name: paulmillr/noble-curves
catalog.build_complexity: vanilla, drop-in — audited ESM, zero deps
catalog.works_with_prana: yes — secp256k1 signing for PRANA txs
catalog.works_with_melek: yes — secp256k1 is also the Graphene curve
catalog.notes: Audited secp256k1 + ed25519. The repo's `pool/www/walletgen/vendor/secp256k1.mjs` is clean-room and derivation-only (no signing). noble-curves is the drop-in if signing is ever needed client-side.

catalog.name: paulmillr/noble-hashes
catalog.build_complexity: vanilla, drop-in — audited ESM, zero deps
catalog.notes: Companion to noble-curves: sha256/sha512/keccak/ripemd160/pbkdf2. Covers everything Graphene key derivation needs.

catalog.name: bitcoinjs/bip39
catalog.build_complexity: vanilla-ish — npm package, needs a bundler for browser use (Buffer polyfill)
catalog.notes: ISC is permissive. Heavier browser story than scure-bip39 because of node Buffer assumptions.

catalog.name: bitcoinjs/bitcoinjs-lib
catalog.build_complexity: needs a bundler for browser use

catalog.name: Alethio/ethereum-lite-explorer
catalog.last_active: 2023-01-04 (last push); last release v1.0.0-beta.10, 2020-04-29; not archived

For a young chain like PRANA that is largely fine.

catalog.name: wevm/mipd
catalog.build_complexity: VANILLA, DROP-IN — a ~2KB dependency-free ESM store for EIP-6963 multi-wallet discovery; no React, no build step
catalog.notes: THE PICK for this repo. `kulaswap/app.mjs` currently does `if (!window.ethereum)` + `new ethers.BrowserProvider(window.ethereum)` — the legacy single-injected-provider path, which silently picks the wrong wallet when a user has more than one extension. mipd fixes exactly that with an EIP-6963 provider list, and it is small enough to vendor as one file alongside the existing `pool/www/walletgen/vendor/` pattern. EIP-6963 itself is ~30 lines of `window.addEventListener('eip6963:announceProvider')`, so this can also simply be hand-written in house style.

catalog.build_complexity: vanilla-capable — ships a browser ESM/UMD build; ALREADY A DEPENDENCY of this repo (ethers 6.16.0 in package.json)

As of 2025-08-25 it is under the Reown Community License, which: (a) assigns Reown ownership of any modifications or derivative works you make; (b) REQUIRES as a material condition that all use connect to Reown's proprietary gateway and forbids circumventing it; (c) caps free use at 2,500,000 monthly RPCs / 500 MAU before a paid commercial licence is required; (d) mandates a 'Portions (c) 2025 Reown, Inc.' notice and their branding on redistribution. Incompatible with a self-sovereign chain stack. Do not adopt.

Anything in this catalogue that 'just uses WalletConnect' inherits these terms — that includes the default configs of RainbowKit, ConnectKit, web3-onboard and thirdweb. If mobile-wallet support is wanted without this dependency, the options are injected/EIP-6963 only, or a self-hosted relay.
